prompt: In MESI, a core holds a line and wants to write it without sending any request to other caches. Which state must the line be in (before the write)? Use the lesson's textbook stable-state protocol with serialised coherence transactions and no eviction or intervening accesses.

options.explanation: S means other caches may hold copies; they must be invalidated (BusUpgr) before writing.
An invalid line isn't usable; a write needs a BusRdX to fetch it with ownership.
Correct. E means this is the only copy and it is clean, so the core can switch to M silently. (A line already in M can of course be written again silently too.)
Owned is a MOESI state meaning dirty *and* shared; other copies exist, so a write must invalidate them.

workedExample:
A write needs exclusive ownership. Check each state:

| State | Others have it? | Write needs |
|---|---|---|
| M | no | nothing |
| E | no | nothing (→ M) |
| S | maybe | BusUpgr |
| I | ? | BusRdX |

E is the state that exists exactly to make "read then write private data" cost one request instead of two.
